<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4bcc4df6496ef2b327739b65c7f2fa2ff4f304e0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f14ef9e7884fbca210f647c5b4bd87b833deadce` — the merge of head `0a8846cd638233e4b47e94ea91bc44a3fff4bd7a` into base `4bcc4df6496ef2b327739b65c7f2fa2ff4f304e0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f14ef9e7884fbca210f647c5b4bd87b833deadce && git checkout f14ef9e7884fbca210f647c5b4bd87b833deadce
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4bcc4df6496ef2b327739b65c7f2fa2ff4f304e0 0a8846cd638233e4b47e94ea91bc44a3fff4bd7a && git checkout -B drift-repro 4bcc4df6496ef2b327739b65c7f2fa2ff4f304e0 && git merge --no-ff 0a8846cd638233e4b47e94ea91bc44a3fff4bd7a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4bcc4df6496ef2b327739b65c7f2fa2ff4f304e0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4bcc4df6496ef2b327739b65c7f2fa2ff4f304e0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · #25575 · `domain:spec` seat 2 (seat post #18549) · `sunhaolin` · session `session_01PC4NPXPgPmpDRG9DdDnyXT` · 2026-10-24T22:13Z · head `0a8846cd63` · report `6388606923` and addendum `6390006109` (on #25575; cloud session `session_017Eg8KpUtdKh6r8YTPjbhod`) · seat review at `TIER_DEFAULT`. The change is a narrowing (`security`, BREAKING), and the path limb hits (`packages/spec/src/security/**`). So a same-shape `## Contract review` PASS at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the landing head is owed, and `needs:contract-review` is added in this stroke.

1. **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #25575`, title `feat(spec,lint)!:`. The `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` and `Ruling-ref: 6377890121 … ; retriage 6382861731` lines are line-initial in the body and in the changeset (`@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/lint` `minor`, BREAKING section, ADR-0087 marker registering both entries). 18 files, +593/−20. `check-governed-merges --pr 25707`: NOT governed. No `content/docs/releases/**`.
2. **The ruling, measured on the diff.** Letter A of `6377890121`, under `6377842908`: keep Modify All as the write bypass for edit, delete and transfer, refuse the pair at publish and in lint, and name the route for "edit all, delete none".
   - **Schema:** `checkScopeAgainstSuperUserBits` gains the arm `modifyAllRecords === true && allowDelete === false`, giving one `custom` issue at `allowDelete`, wildcard `*` included. It rides the #16870 refinement, so `EffectiveObjectPermissionSchema` stays tolerant.
   - **Mechanism the claim did not foresee:** `allowDelete` has `.default(false)`, so the parsed output of `{ modifyAllRecords: true }` was itself the refused pair. `materializeModifyAllDelete`, a `z.preprocess` stage outside the residue stage (with `shape` read through), writes `true` into an omitted key only. `parse(parse(x)) = parse(x)` is pinned.
   - **Lint:** `security-modify-all-delete-withheld` (error) in the security-posture family, reaching only the unparsed doors, the same posture as `security-owd-alias`.
   - **Runtime:** unchanged. `MODIFY_ALL_WRITE_KEYS` is untouched, and there is no `editAllRecords` key.
3. **The route, measured.** On a booted stack (`bootStack`, a temporary test, not committed), with a `criteria` rule `accessLevel: 'edit'` to a position on a `public_read` object:
   - update is 200 and delete is 403, on both old and newly inserted rows, and create is 403;
   - control: `condition: 'true'` is logged "not served … match-all-criteria", and the same update is refused at the record.
   The docs recipe and every prescription name `record.id != ''`, never a literal `true`. That matches ADR-0111 D3 (no share branch in `checkDelete`).
4. **Data at rest.**
   - D2 `permission-modify-all-allow-delete-false-to-true` is retired from the load path, with `retiredAfter: '18.1.0'` = the latest published `@objectstack/spec` (read this round). It is lossless against the runtime: the holder could always delete.
   - D3 `permission-modify-all-allow-delete-false-refused` links it through `conversionIds`.
   - **Premise corrected in patch round 1:** HotCRM *authors* the pair. At `src/sales/profiles/sales-manager.profile.ts:57` (`crm_forecast`; seat read at HotCRM `8a14b56`, dev at `a4b3560`), the 17.1 artifact's entry is authored, not a filled default. The docblock, the fixture comment and the PR body now say so. The showcase `showcase_ops` stays the filled-default instance.
5. **Gates.** `ci-failure --pr 25707` GREEN: 42 check-runs on `0a8846cd63`, all completed, none failed.
   - The round-1 red (cli integration, a tracker id `#4001` in the D3 `reason`) was reproduced on `c5b702ced` before the fix.
   - At `0a8846cd6`: cli unit + integration 499 / 6286; spec 719 / 21788 and `test:repo` 79 / 1269; lint 161 / 7274; metadata 64 / 906; 116/116 derived, `--ran` 0 NOT-MEASURED.
   - Round-1 consumers stand: runtime, core, verify, metadata-core, metadata-protocol, rest, plugin-security, with `test:repo` where declared.
   - The dogfood battery ran at `c5b702ced` (295 files / 2520 tests, exit 0). It was not re-run after a strings-and-comments push; accepted.
   - **Ablations**, predicted and met, each restored blob-identical: (a) the refinement arm off gives 2 of 101 red (the explicit refusal, the wildcard); (b) the materialise stage off gives 2 of 101 red (omitted key parses to `true`, idempotency).
6. **Open questions** (answered in the patch round): (1) materialise `true` for an omitted key, **A**: the minimum mechanism that makes the refusal idempotent. (2) Keep the lint arm, **A**: the director's state comment `6377871867` names it ("at publish and in lint"). (3) `os migrate meta` replays the D2 entry, **A**: D3 `conversionIds` carries the judgment.
7. **Deviations accepted.**
   - Round 1 skipped the cli integration project. The dev's reading "the diff touches no CLI spawn entry" was wrong, which the dev states in the addendum. Fixed and re-measured.
   - `mcp_calls` 2, both reads; relay writes 3.
   - Out of scope, no carrier: `GetObjectPermissionsResponseSchema.permissions` inherits the refusal through the authoring schema, as it already inherits the #16870 scope refusals.
8. **Downstream, carried by the seat:** at this PR's merge, the seat files a HotCRM card for `sales_manager.crm_forecast`. The choice is HotCRM's: drop `allowDelete: false` to keep Modify All, or move to the edit-share route. Its deployed 17.1 artifact keeps loading through D2.
9. **Landing.** Not governed, 613 changed lines. Once a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` PASS is on record and every check on the then-current head is green, the seat sends `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the relay. At landing, the seat re-checks that `retiredAfter` still names the latest published release.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0a8846cd638233e4b47e94ea91bc44a3fff4bd7a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: schema face (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`) — recogniser hits `packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.permission-modify-all-allow-delete-false-refused.ts`, `packages/spec/src/security/permission.test.ts`, `packages/spec/src/shared/retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts`; cited `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, `packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.test.ts`, `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`, `packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/metadata/src/plugin-artifact-forward-conversion.test.ts`; prose `.changeset/25575-modify-all-allow-delete.md`, `content/docs/permissions/*.mdx`, `content/docs/references/{api/protocol,security/permission}.mdx`.

### ① Derived judgments

- Declaration matches the diff. `ObjectPermissionSchema` now refuses an authored `allowDelete: false` beside `modifyAllRecords: true` at path `allowDelete` (wildcard included) inside `checkScopeAgainstSuperUserBits`; nothing is widened. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` are the right declarations for a published key that loses an accepted shape.
- Ruling conformance. Letter A (6377890121 under 6377842908, retriage 6382861731): schema refusal at publish, lint refusal (`security-modify-all-delete-withheld`, error, unparsed intakes only), runtime and `MODIFY_ALL_WRITE_KEYS` untouched, docs name the sharing-rule route for "edit every record, delete none". All four present; Salesforce Modify All semantics kept.
- The `materializeModifyAllDelete` preprocess is the minimal mechanism, not a widening. `allowDelete` carries `.default(false)`, so a refinement alone would refuse its own output on the second parse. Writing `true` into an omitted key records what the evaluator already grants and keeps the parse idempotent. Only the authoring schema takes the stage; `EffectiveObjectPermissionSchema` stays tolerant (authorable/wire split). The `shape` read-through is preserved for the schema walkers, which the baseline `out` → `out.out` site moves confirm.
- ADR-0087 disposition complete: D2 conversion `permission-modify-all-allow-delete-false-to-true` (toMajor 18, order 75, `retiredFromLoadPath: true`, `retiredAfter: '18.1.0'`, fixture with one notice, idempotent) plus D3 semantic entry with acceptanceCriteria naming the D2 replay judgment for `os migrate meta --from 17`. Marker registered in the changeset.
- Docs recipe is measured, not asserted: `criteria` rule with `condition: "record.id != ''"` and `accessLevel: 'edit'` (update 200, delete 403 on a booted stack); the `condition: 'true'` trap (empty filter, never served) is documented beside it.
- Dogfood battery ran at `c5b702ced` (295/2520, exit 0); the push to `0a8846cd6` is strings-only and the seat accepted it (6390192995). Ablations (a)(b) each turn 2 of 101 red, restored.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/lint` minor, with `!` and a BREAKING banner carrying Before/Now/Fix. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` ⇒ at least minor, so the level is right. The 54 check runs on the head are all success or skipped (Test Core 1–6, Build Core, Build Docs, Dogfood Regression Gate, Type Check, Lint, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, claim gates).

### ③ Boundary flags

- `retiredAfter: '18.1.0'` must track the latest published spec at landing: if a spec release cuts before this merges, the value moves (seat already notes this).
- Producer in another repo: HotCRM `src/sales/profiles/sales-manager.profile.ts` authors the pair on `crm_forecast`; its 17.1 artifact gets the D2 rewrite, its next rebuild meets the refusal. Seat files the HotCRM card at merge.
- `GetObjectPermissionsResponseSchema.permissions` inherits the refusal (authoring schema reused on the response side); noted in Acceptance, no client in repo sends the pair.
- `os migrate meta --from 17` replays D2 and keeps the delete grant; the D3 entry is the judgment owed. Acceptable under letter A since no access decision changes.
